title.zh: 卷十八 志第八 禮樂八
title.raw: 卷十八 志第八 禮樂八 Volume 18 Treatises 8: Rites and Music 8

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 皇帝納皇后。

translations.literal: The emperor receives an empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor takes an empress.

sentences.zh: 制命太尉為使，宗正卿為副，吏部承以戒之。

translations.literal: By edict the Grand Commandant was appointed envoy, the Director of the Imperial Clan as deputy, and the Ministry of Personnel conveyed the admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named the Grand Commandant envoy and the Director of the Imperial Clan deputy; the Ministry of Personnel delivered the ritual cautions.

sentences.zh: 前一日，有司展縣、設桉、陳車輿于太極殿廷，如元日。

translations.literal: On the previous day the relevant offices hung the bells, set the tables, and arrayed the carriages in the court of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, as on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, officials hung bells, set tables, and lined up carriages in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate court, as on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 文武九品、朝集、蕃客之位，皆如冠禮。

translations.literal: The stations of civil and military officials of nine ranks, assembly attendees, and foreign guests were all as at the capping rite.
translations.idiomatic: Placement of civil and military officials through nine ranks, assembly guests, and foreign envoys followed the capping rite.

sentences.zh: 設使者受命位於大橫街南道東，西上，副少退，北面。

translations.literal: The envoy's place to receive the mandate was set east of the road on the south side of Great Cross Street, west at the right, the deputy slightly withdrawn, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy's mandate station lay east of the road on the south side of Great Cross Street, west at the right; the deputy stood slightly back, facing north.

sentences.zh: 侍中請「中嚴」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant requested "mid-court vigil."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant called for mid-court vigil.

sentences.zh: 羣臣入就位。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers entered and took their places.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers entered to their stations.

sentences.zh: 使、副入，立於門外道東，西面。

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy entered and stood east of the gate outside the road, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy entered and stood east of the outer gate road, facing west.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎引幡、節，中書侍郎引制書桉，立於左延明門內道北，西面北上。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Yellow Gate led the banners and staff; the Vice Director of the Secretariat led the edict table; they stood north of the road inside the left Yanming Gate, facing west with north at the right.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Gate Vice Director led banners and staff; the Secretariat Vice Director led the edict table; both stood north of the road inside the left Yanming Gate, facing west, north at the right.

sentences.zh: 乃奏「外辦」。

translations.literal: Then they reported "the outer rites are ready."
translations.idiomatic: They then announced that the outer rites were ready.

sentences.zh: 皇帝衮冕御輿，出自西房，即御座。

translations.literal: The emperor in dragon robes and coronet rode the imperial carriage, came out from the west chamber, and took the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: In dragon robes and coronet the emperor rode out from the west chamber and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 使、副入，就位。

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy entered and took their places.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy entered to their stations.

sentences.zh: 典儀曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies said: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: " All those in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " All present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 侍中前承制，降詣使者東北，西面曰：「有制。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant came forward to receive the edict, descended to the envoy's northeast, faced west, and said: "There is an edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant advanced to take the edict, went down to the envoy's northeast, faced west, and said: "By edict.

sentences.zh: 」使、副再拜。

translations.literal: " The envoy and deputy bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " Envoy and deputy bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 侍中宣制曰：「納某官某氏女為皇后，命公等持節行納采等禮。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant proclaimed the edict: "Take the daughter of such-and-such an official and clan as empress; we command you to bear the staff and perform betrothal and the other rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant read: "Take the daughter of Official So-and-so of Clan Such-and-such as empress; you are ordered to bear the staff and conduct betrothal and the following rites.

sentences.zh: 」使、副又拜。

translations.literal: " The envoy and deputy bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: " Envoy and deputy bowed again.

sentences.zh: 主節立於使者東北，西面，以節授黃門侍郎，侍郎以授使者，付于主節，立於後。

translations.literal: The chief staff-bearer stood northeast of the envoy, faced west, handed the staff to the Yellow Gate Vice Director; the Vice Director handed it to the envoy, who gave it to the chief staff-bearer, who stood behind.
translations.idiomatic: The chief staff-bearer stood northeast of the envoy, faced west, passed the staff to the Yellow Gate Vice Director, who passed it to the envoy; the envoy gave it to the chief staff-bearer, who stood behind.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎引制書桉立於使者東北，以制書授使者，置於桉。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Vice Director led the edict table to stand northeast of the envoy, handed the edict to the envoy, and set it on the table.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Vice Director brought the edict table northeast of the envoy, handed over the edict, and set it on the table.

sentences.zh: 典儀曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies said: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: " All those in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " All present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 使、副出，持節者前導，持桉者次之。

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy departed; the staff-bearer led, the table-bearer followed.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy left; the staff-bearer went first, the table-bearer after.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏「禮畢」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported "the rite is complete."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announced the rite complete.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入，在位者以次出。

translations.literal: The emperor entered; those in attendance departed in order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withdrew; those present left in order.

sentences.zh: 初，使、副乘輅，鼓吹備而不作，從者乘車以從。

translations.literal: At first the envoy and deputy rode in the ceremonial chariot; the musicians were ready but did not play; attendants followed in carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Initially envoy and deputy rode the ceremonial chariot with musicians present but silent; attendants followed in carriages.

sentences.zh: 其制書以油絡網犢車載之。

translations.literal: The edict was carried on an oil-net covered calf cart.
translations.idiomatic: The edict rode on a calf cart covered with oiled netting.

sentences.zh: 其日大昕，使、副至于次，主人受於廟若寢。

translations.literal: At dawn that day the envoy and deputy reached the lodge; the host received them at the ancestral temple or private apartment.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the envoy and deputy reached the lodge; the host received them at the temple or inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 布神席於室戶外之西，莞筵紛純，加藻席畫純，南向，右彫几。

translations.literal: A spirit mat was spread west of the outer door of the chamber, rush mat with black border, over it an painted mat with patterned border, facing south, with carved armrest to the right.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit mat was laid west of the chamber's outer door: rush mat with black border, painted mat on top, facing south, carved armrest to the right.

sentences.zh: 使、副立於門西，北上，持幡、節者立於北，少退，制桉立於南，執鴈者又在其南，皆東面。

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy stood west of the gate, north at the right; those with banners and staff stood north, slightly back; the edict table south; the goose-bearer still farther south—all facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy stood west of the gate, north at the right; banner and staff bearers north, slightly back; edict table south; goose-bearer farther south—all east-facing.

sentences.zh: 主人立於大門內，西面。

translations.literal: The host stood inside the great gate, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The host stood inside the main gate, facing west.

sentences.zh: 儐者北面，受命於左，出立於門東，西面，曰：「敢請事。

translations.literal: The usher faced north, received the command on the left, went out and stood east of the gate, faced west, and said: "I venture to ask your business.
translations.idiomatic: The usher faced north, took orders on the left, went out east of the gate, faced west, and said: "May I ask your purpose?

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「某奉制納采。

translations.literal: " The envoy said: "So-and-so, by edict, presents betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy said: "So-and-so, by edict, brings betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 」儐者入告。

translations.literal: " The usher entered to report.
translations.idiomatic: " The usher went in to announce.

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「臣某之女若如人，既蒙制訪，臣某不敢辭。

translations.literal: The host said: "My daughter So-and-so is unworthy; having received the imperial inquiry, I So-and-so dare not decline.
translations.idiomatic: The host said: "My daughter is unworthy; honored by the imperial inquiry, I dare not refuse.

sentences.zh: 」儐者出告，入引主人出，迎使者於大門外之南，北面再拜。

translations.literal: " The usher went out to report, entered, led the host out, and met the envoy south of the outer great gate; the host faced north and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " The usher reported, re-entered, led the host out, and met the envoy south of the main gate; the host faced north and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 使者不答。

translations.literal: The envoy did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy made no reply.

sentences.zh: 主人揖使、副先入，至於階。

translations.literal: The host gestured for the envoy and deputy to enter first, up to the steps.
translations.idiomatic: The host motioned envoy and deputy to enter first, to the steps.

sentences.zh: 使、副入，導以幡、節，桉、鴈從之。

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy entered, led by banners and staff; table and geese followed.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy entered under banners and staff; table and geese followed.

sentences.zh: 幡、節立西階之西，東面；

translations.literal: Banners and staff stood west of the west steps, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: Banners and staff stood west of the west steps, east-facing;

sentences.zh: 使者由階升，立於兩楹間，南面；

translations.literal: the envoy ascended by the steps and stood between the two pillars, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: the envoy mounted the steps and stood between the pillars, south-facing;

sentences.zh: 副在西南，持桉及執鴈者又在西南，皆東面。

translations.literal: the deputy in the southwest; those with the table and geese still farther southwest—all facing east.
translations.idiomatic: the deputy southwest; table and goose bearers farther southwest—all east-facing.

sentences.zh: 主人升阼階，當使者前，北面立。

translations.literal: The host ascended the host steps, stood before the envoy, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The host mounted the host steps and stood before the envoy, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 持桉者以桉進，授使者以制書，節脫衣，使者曰：「有制。

translations.literal: The table-bearer advanced with the table, handed the edict to the envoy; the staff was unwrapped; the envoy said: "There is an edict.
translations.idiomatic: The table-bearer advanced, handed the edict to the envoy; the staff was uncovered; the envoy said: "By edict.

sentences.zh: 」主人再拜。

translations.literal: " The host bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " The host bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 宣制，主人降詣階間，北面，再拜稽首，升，進，北面受制書，以授左右。

translations.literal: The edict was proclaimed; the host descended to the space between the steps, faced north, bowed twice and knocked head to ground, ascended, advanced, faced north to receive the edict, and handed it to attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was read; the host went down between the steps, north-facing, bowed twice and kowtowed, mounted, advanced, received the edict north-facing, and passed it to attendants.

sentences.zh: 使者授鴈，主人再拜，進受鴈，以授左右。

translations.literal: The envoy handed over the geese; the host bowed twice, advanced to receive the geese, and handed them to attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy presented the geese; the host bowed twice, advanced to take them, and passed them to attendants.

sentences.zh: 儐者引答表桉進，立於主人後，少西，以表授主人。

translations.literal: The usher led the reply-table forward, stood behind the host slightly west, and handed the table to the host.
translations.idiomatic: The usher brought the reply-table forward, stood behind the host slightly west, and gave the table to the host.

sentences.zh: 主人進，授使者，退復位，再拜。

translations.literal: The host advanced, handed it to the envoy, withdrew to his place, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The host advanced, gave it to the envoy, returned, and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 節加衣。

translations.literal: The staff was re-wrapped.
translations.idiomatic: The staff was covered again.

sentences.zh: 謁者引使、副降自西階以出。

translations.literal: The usher led the envoy and deputy down the west steps to depart.
translations.idiomatic: The usher led envoy and deputy down the west steps out.

sentences.zh: 制文以版，長一尺二寸，博四寸，厚八分，后家答版亦如之。

translations.literal: The edict text was on a tablet one foot two inches long, four inches wide, and eight lines thick; the empress's family reply tablet was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Edict text was on a tablet one foot two inches long, four inches wide, eight lines thick; the empress's family reply tablet matched.

sentences.zh: 問名。

translations.literal: Inquiry of the name.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry of the name.

sentences.zh: 使者既出，遂立於內門外之西，東面；

translations.literal: After the envoy had gone out, he then stood west of the inner gate outside, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: After the envoy left, he stood west outside the inner gate, east-facing;

sentences.zh: 主人立於內門內東廂，西面。

translations.literal: the host stood in the east wing inside the inner gate, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: the host stood in the east wing inside the inner gate, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 儐者出請事，使者曰：「將加卜筮，奉制問名。

translations.literal: The usher came out to ask business; the envoy said: "Tortoise and milfoil will be applied; by edict I inquire the name.
translations.idiomatic: The usher asked their business; the envoy said: "We shall divine by tortoise and milfoil; by edict I inquire the name.

sentences.zh: 」儐者入告。

translations.literal: " The usher entered to report.
translations.idiomatic: " The usher went in to announce.

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「臣某之子若如人，既蒙制訪，臣某不敢辭。

translations.literal: The host said: "My son So-and-so is unworthy; having received the imperial inquiry, I So-and-so dare not decline.
translations.idiomatic: The host said: "My son is unworthy; honored by the imperial inquiry, I dare not refuse.

sentences.zh: 」儐者出告，入，引主人出，迎使者以入，授主人以制書，答表皆如納采。

translations.literal: " The usher went out to report, entered, led the host out, welcomed the envoy in, and handed the host the edict; the reply table was as at betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: " The usher reported, re-entered, led the host out to welcome the envoy in; edict and reply table followed betrothal.

sentences.zh: 使、副降自西階以出，立於內門外之西，東面；

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy descended the west steps to go out and stood west of the inner gate outside, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy went down the west steps, stood west outside the inner gate, east-facing;

sentences.zh: 主人立於東階下，西向。

translations.literal: the host stood below the east steps, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: the host stood below the east steps, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 儐者出請事，使者曰：「禮畢。

translations.literal: The usher came out to ask business; the envoy said: "The rite is complete.
translations.idiomatic: The usher asked business; the envoy said: "The rite is finished.

sentences.zh: 」儐者入告，主人曰：「某公奉制至於某之室，某有先人之禮，請禮從者。

translations.literal: " The usher entered to report; the host said: "Lord So-and-so has come by edict to my house; I have my ancestors' rite—please treat the followers.
translations.idiomatic: " The usher announced; the host said: "Lord So-and-so has come by edict; I have ancestral hospitality—please honor the entourage.

sentences.zh: 」儐者出告，使者曰：「某既得將事，敢辭。

translations.literal: " The usher went out to report; the envoy said: "Having received commission for the main affair, I venture to decline.
translations.idiomatic: " The usher reported; the envoy said: "Commissioned for the main rite, I must decline.

sentences.zh: 」儐者入告，主人曰：「先人之禮，敢固以請。

translations.literal: " The usher entered to report; the host said: "My ancestors' rite—I firmly venture to request it.
translations.idiomatic: " The usher announced; the host said: "Ancestral hospitality—I insist.

sentences.zh: 」儐者出告，使者曰：「某辭不得命，敢不從。

translations.literal: " The usher went out to report; the envoy said: "I declined but received no release—I dare not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: " The usher reported; the envoy said: "I declined but was not excused—I cannot refuse.

sentences.zh: 」儐者入告，遂引主人升立於序端。

translations.literal: " The usher entered to report, then led the host up to stand at the end of the wing.
translations.idiomatic: " The usher announced and led the host up to the wing end.

sentences.zh: 掌事者徹几，設二筵東上。

translations.literal: The attendants removed the armrest and set two mats with east at the top.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants removed the armrest and set two mats, east at the top.

sentences.zh: 設甒醴於東房西牖下，加杓冪，坫在尊北；

translations.literal: Black-cloth wine was set under the west window of the east chamber, ladle and cover added; the stand was north of the jar;
translations.idiomatic: Black-cloth wine was placed under the east chamber's west window, ladle and cover added; the stand north of the jar;

sentences.zh: 實觶二，角柶二，籩、豆各一，實以脯醢，在坫北。

translations.literal: two goblets, two horn ladles, one basket and one dish each filled with dried meat and hash—north of the stand.
translations.idiomatic: two goblets, two horn ladles, one basket and one dish of dried meat and hash—north of the stand.

sentences.zh: 又設洗於東南。

translations.literal: A lavabo was also set in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: A lavabo was set in the southeast as well.

sentences.zh: 主人降迎使者，西面揖，先入。

translations.literal: The host descended to meet the envoy, bowed west-facing, and entered first.
translations.idiomatic: The host came down to meet the envoy, west-facing bow, and entered first.

sentences.zh: 使、副入門而左，主人入門而右。

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy entered the gate to the left; the host entered the gate to the right.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy entered left of the gate; the host entered right.

sentences.zh: 至階，主人曰：「請某位升。

translations.literal: At the steps the host said: "Please ascend to your place.
translations.idiomatic: At the steps the host said: "Please mount to your seat.

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「某敢辭。

translations.literal: " The envoy said: "I venture to decline.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy said: "I must decline.

sentences.zh: 」主人又曰：「固請某位升。

translations.literal: " The host again said: "I firmly request that you ascend to your place.
translations.idiomatic: " The host again said: "I insist you take your seat.

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「某敢固辭。

translations.literal: " The envoy said: "I firmly venture to decline.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 」主人又曰：「終請某位升。

translations.literal: " The host again said: "Finally I request that you ascend to your place.
translations.idiomatic: " The host said finally: "I must ask you to mount.

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「敢終辭。

translations.literal: " The envoy said: "I dare finally decline.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy said he must finally decline.

sentences.zh: 」主人升自阼階，使、副升自西階，北面立。

translations.literal: " The host ascended by the host steps; the envoy and deputy ascended by the west steps and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: " The host mounted the host steps; envoy and deputy mounted the west steps, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 主人阼階上，北面再拜。

translations.literal: On the host steps the host faced north and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: On the host steps the host bowed twice north-facing.

sentences.zh: 受几於序端。

translations.literal: He received the armrest at the wing end.
translations.idiomatic: He received the armrest at the wing end.

sentences.zh: 掌事者內拂几三，奉兩端西北向以進。

translations.literal: An attendant dusted the armrest inward three times and advanced northwest-facing with both ends.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant dusted the armrest inward three times and advanced, both ends to the northwest.

sentences.zh: 主人東南向，外拂几三，振袂，內執之。

translations.literal: The host faced southeast, dusted outward three times, shook his sleeves, and held it inward.
translations.idiomatic: The host faced southeast, dusted outward three times, shook his sleeves, and held it inward.

sentences.zh: 掌事者一人又執几以從，主人進，西北向。

translations.literal: Another attendant also held an armrest and followed; the host advanced, northwest-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Another attendant carried a second armrest and followed; the host advanced northwest-facing.

sentences.zh: 使者序進，迎受於筵前，東南向以俟。

translations.literal: The envoy advanced in order, received it before the mat southeast-facing, and waited.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy advanced in order, received it before the mat southeast-facing, and waited.

sentences.zh: 主人還東階上，北面再拜送。

translations.literal: The host returned to the east steps, faced north, and bowed twice in send-off.
translations.idiomatic: The host returned to the east steps, north-facing, and bowed twice sending it off.

sentences.zh: 使者以几跪進，北面跪，各設於坐左，退於西階上，北面東上，答拜，立於階西，東面南上。

translations.literal: The envoy advanced with the armrest kneeling, faced north kneeling, each set to the left of the seat, withdrew to the west steps north-facing with east at the top, returned the bow, and stood west of the steps east-facing with south at the top.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy knelt forward with the armrest, north-facing on his knees, set each left of the seat, withdrew to the west steps north-facing east at top, returned the bow, and stood west of the steps east-facing south at top.

sentences.zh: 贊者二人俱升，取觶降，盥手，洗觶，升，實醴，加柶於觶，覆之，面葉，出房，南面。

translations.literal: Two assistants both ascended, took the goblets down, washed hands, rinsed the goblets, ascended, filled with wine, placed ladles on the goblets, covered them handle-out, came out of the chamber south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Two assistants ascended, took goblets down, washed hands and goblets, mounted, filled with wine, set ladles handle-out on the goblets, left the chamber south-facing.

sentences.zh: 主人受醴，面柄，進使者筵前西，北面立。

translations.literal: The host received the wine handle-out, advanced west of the envoy's mat, and stood north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The host took the wine handle-out, advanced west of the envoy's mat, and stood north-facing.

sentences.zh: 又贊者執觶以從。

translations.literal: Another assistant followed with a goblet.
translations.idiomatic: Another assistant followed with a goblet.

sentences.zh: 使者西階上，北面，各一拜，序進筵前東，南面。

translations.literal: On the west steps the envoy faced north; each bowed once, advanced in order east of the mat south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: On the west steps the envoy faced north; each bowed once and advanced in order east of the mat, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 主人又以次授醴，使者受，俱復西階上位。

translations.literal: The host again handed wine in order; the envoy received; both returned to places on the west steps.
translations.idiomatic: The host handed wine in turn; the envoy received; both returned to the west steps.

sentences.zh: 主人退，復東階上，北面一拜送。

translations.literal: The host withdrew, returned to the east steps, and north-facing bowed once in send-off.
translations.idiomatic: The host withdrew to the east steps and bowed once north-facing in send-off.

sentences.zh: 掌事者以次薦脯醢於筵前。

translations.literal: Attendants in order presented dried meat and hash before the mats.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants presented dried meat and hash before the mats in order.

sentences.zh: 使者各進，升筵，皆坐，左執觶，右取脯，擩於醢，祭於籩、豆之間，各以柶祭醴三，始扱一祭，又扱再祭，興；

translations.literal: Each envoy advanced, mounted the mat, all sat, left hand on the goblet, right hand took dried meat, dipped in hash, sacrificed between basket and dish; each with the ladle sacrificed to the wine three times—first dip one sacrifice, dip again two sacrifices—then rose;
translations.idiomatic: Each envoy advanced, mounted the mat, sat, left on the goblet, right took dried meat, dipped hash, offered between basket and dish; each ladle-offered to the wine three times—first dip once, second dip twice—then rose;

sentences.zh: 各以柶兼諸觶上，躐降筵於西階上，俱北面坐，啐醴，建柶，各奠觶於薦，遂拜，執觶，興。

translations.literal: each placed the ladle across the goblet, stepped down the mat at the west steps, both north-facing sat, tasted the wine, set the ladle upright, each set the goblet on the offering, then bowed, took the goblet, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: each laid the ladle across the goblet, stepped down at the west steps, sat north-facing, tasted wine, set the ladle upright, placed each goblet on the offering, bowed, took the goblet, and rose.

sentences.zh: 主人答拜。

translations.literal: The host returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: The host returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 使者進，升筵坐，各奠觶於薦東。

translations.literal: The envoy advanced, mounted the mat and sat, each set the goblet east of the offering.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy advanced, sat on the mat, and set each goblet east of the offering.

sentences.zh: 降筵，序立於西階上，東面南上。

translations.literal: They descended the mat and stood in order on the west steps, east-facing with south at the top.
translations.idiomatic: They left the mat and stood in order on the west steps, east-facing, south at the top.

sentences.zh: 掌事者牽馬入，陳於門內，三分庭一在南，北首西上。

translations.literal: Attendants led horses in and arrayed them inside the gate, one-third of the courtyard south, heads north with west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants led horses in and lined them inside the gate, one-third of the court to the south, heads north, west at the top.

sentences.zh: 又掌事者奉幣篚，升自東階，以授主人，受於序端，進西面位。

translations.literal: Another attendant bore the coin baskets, ascended the east steps, handed them to the host, who received them at the wing end and advanced to the west-facing place.
translations.idiomatic: Another attendant brought coin baskets up the east steps to the host, who received them at the wing end and advanced west-facing.

sentences.zh: 掌事者一人，又奉幣篚，立於主人之後。

translations.literal: Another attendant bore a coin basket and stood behind the host.
translations.idiomatic: Another attendant with a coin basket stood behind the host.

sentences.zh: 使者西階上，俱北面再拜。

translations.literal: On the west steps the envoy, all north-facing, bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: On the west steps the envoy party bowed twice, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 主人進詣楹間，南面立，使者序進，立於主人之西，俱南面。

translations.literal: The host advanced to between the pillars, stood south-facing; the envoy advanced in order west of the host, all south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The host advanced between the pillars, south-facing; the envoy advanced in order west of him, all south-facing.

sentences.zh: 主人以幣篚授使者，使者受，退立於西階上，東面。

translations.literal: The host handed the coin basket to the envoy; the envoy received it and withdrew to the west steps, east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The host gave the coin basket to the envoy; the envoy took it and withdrew to the west steps, east-facing.

sentences.zh: 執幣者又以授主人，主人受以授使副，使副受之，退立於使者之北，俱東面。

translations.literal: The coin-bearer again handed to the host; the host received and handed to the deputy; the deputy received and withdrew north of the envoy, all east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The coin-bearer passed it again to the host, who gave it to the deputy; the deputy took it and stood north of the envoy, all east-facing.

sentences.zh: 主人還東階上，北面再拜送。

translations.literal: The host returned to the east steps, north-facing, and bowed twice in send-off.
translations.idiomatic: The host returned to the east steps and bowed twice north-facing in send-off.

sentences.zh: 使者降自西階，從者訝受幣篚。

translations.literal: The envoy descended the west steps; followers received the coin baskets.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy went down the west steps; followers took the coin baskets.

sentences.zh: 使者當庭實揖馬以出，牽馬者從出。

translations.literal: In the courtyard the envoy gestured to the horses and departed; the horse-leaders followed out.
translations.idiomatic: In the court the envoy gestured the horses out; grooms followed.

sentences.zh: 使者出大門外之西，東面立。

translations.literal: The envoy stood east of the outer great gate, east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy stood east outside the main gate, east-facing.

sentences.zh: 從者訝受馬。

translations.literal: Followers received the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Followers took the horses.

sentences.zh: 主人出門東，西面再拜送。

translations.literal: The host went out east of the gate, west-facing, and bowed twice in send-off.
translations.idiomatic: The host went out east of the gate, west-facing, and bowed twice seeing them off.

sentences.zh: 使者退，主人入，立於東階下，西面。

translations.literal: The envoy withdrew; the host entered and stood below the east steps, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy left; the host entered and stood below the east steps, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 儐者告於主人曰：「賓不顧矣。

translations.literal: The usher reported to the host: "The guest has not looked back."
translations.idiomatic: The usher told the host: "The guest did not look back."

sentences.zh: 」主人反於寢。

translations.literal: " The host returned to the private apartment.
translations.idiomatic: " The host returned to the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 使者奉答表詣闕。

translations.literal: The envoy bore the reply table to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy carried the reply table to court.

sentences.zh: 納吉。

translations.literal: Acceptance of the auspicious divination.
translations.idiomatic: Acceptance of the auspicious divination.

sentences.zh: 使者之辭曰：「加諸卜筮，占曰日從，制使某也入告。

translations.literal: The envoy's words: "Having added tortoise and milfoil divination, the omen reads the day follows; by edict So-and-so enters to report."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said: "After tortoise and milfoil, the omen is favorable; by edict So-and-so reports."

sentences.zh: 」主人之辭曰：「臣某之女若如人，龜筮云吉，臣預在焉，臣某謹奉典制。

translations.literal: The host's words: "My daughter So-and-so is unworthy; tortoise and milfoil say auspicious; I was present; I So-and-so respectfully follow the canonical statutes."
translations.idiomatic: The host said: "My daughter is unworthy; the divination is auspicious; I was present and follow the statutes."

sentences.zh: 」其餘皆如納采。

translations.literal: The rest was all as at betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed betrothal.

sentences.zh: 納徵。

translations.literal: Delivery of the bride-price.
translations.idiomatic: Delivery of the bride-price.

sentences.zh: 其日，使者至于主人之門外，執事者入，布幕於內門之外，玄纁束陳於幕上，六馬陳於幕南，北首西上。

translations.literal: That day the envoy reached outside the host's gate; attendants entered and spread a canopy outside the inner gate; black and red bundles were set on the canopy; six horses were arrayed south of the canopy, heads north with west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: That day the envoy arrived at the host's gate; attendants spread a canopy outside the inner gate, laid black-red bundles on it, and arrayed six horses south of the canopy, heads north, west at the top.

sentences.zh: 執事者奉穀珪以匵，俟於幕東，西面。

translations.literal: Attendants bore the grain tally in a case and waited east of the canopy, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants held the grain tally in a case east of the canopy, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 謁者引使者及主人立於大門之內外。

translations.literal: The usher led the envoy and host to stand inside and outside the great gate.
translations.idiomatic: The usher placed envoy and host inside and outside the main gate.

sentences.zh: 儐者進受命，出請事。

translations.literal: The usher advanced to receive the command and came out to ask business.
translations.idiomatic: The usher took orders and came out to ask their business.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「某奉制納徵。

translations.literal: The envoy said: "So-and-so, by edict, delivers the bride-price."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said: "So-and-so, by edict, brings the bride-price."

sentences.zh: 」儐者入告，主人曰：「奉制賜臣以重禮，臣某祗奉典制。

translations.literal: The usher entered to report; the host said: "Having received the edict's gift of heavy presents, I So-and-so respectfully follow the canonical statutes."
translations.idiomatic: The usher announced; the host said: "Honored by the edict's heavy gifts, I follow the statutes."

sentences.zh: 」儐者出告，入，引主人出，迎使者入。

translations.literal: The usher went out to report, entered, led the host out, and welcomed the envoy in.
translations.idiomatic: The usher reported, re-entered, led the host out, and welcomed the envoy in.

sentences.zh: 執事者坐，啟匵取珪，加於玄纁。

translations.literal: Attendants sat, opened the case, took the tally, and placed it on the black and red bundles.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants sat, opened the case, took the tally, and set it on the bundles.

sentences.zh: 牽馬者從入，三分庭一在南，北首西上。

translations.literal: Horse-leaders followed in; one-third of the courtyard south, heads north with west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: Grooms followed in; one-third of the court to the south, heads north, west at the top.

sentences.zh: 執珪者在馬西，俱北面。

translations.literal: The tally-bearer stood west of the horses, all north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The tally-bearer stood west of the horses, all north-facing.

sentences.zh: 其餘皆如納采。

translations.literal: The rest was all as at betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed betrothal.

sentences.zh: 冊后。

translations.literal: Investiture of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture of the empress.

sentences.zh: 前一日，守宮設使者次於后氏大門外之西，尚舍設尚宮以下次於后氏閤外道西，東向，障以行帷。

translations.literal: On the previous day the palace guards set the envoy's lodge west outside the empress's family great gate; the Imperial Household set lodges for Palace Ladies and below west of the empress's family gate lane outside the road, east-facing, screened by traveling curtains.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, guards set the envoy's lodge west outside the empress's family gate; the Imperial Household set lodges for palace ladies west of the lane outside the gate, east-facing, behind traveling screens.

sentences.zh: 其日，臨軒命使，如納采。

translations.literal: That day the emperor faced the hall to appoint the envoy, as at betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor appointed the envoy at the hall, as at betrothal.

sentences.zh: 奉禮設使者位於大門外之西，東向；

translations.literal: Directors of Ritual set the envoy's place west outside the great gate, east-facing;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual directors set the envoy west outside the main gate, east-facing;

sentences.zh: 使副及內侍位於使者之南，舉冊桉及寶綬者在南，差退，持節者在使者之北，少退，俱東向。

translations.literal: deputy and eunuchs south of the envoy; those with investiture table and seal cord farther south, slightly back; staff-bearer north of the envoy, slightly back—all east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: deputy and eunuchs south of the envoy; investiture table and seal cord bearers farther south, slightly back; staff-bearer north of the envoy, slightly back—all east-facing.

sentences.zh: 設主人位於大門外之南，北面。

translations.literal: The host's place was set south outside the great gate, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The host's station lay south outside the main gate, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 使者以下及主人位於內門外，亦如之。

translations.literal: Envoy, deputy, and host inside the inner gate were also as above.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the inner gate, envoy, deputy, and host were placed the same way.

sentences.zh: 設內謁者監位於內門外主人之南，西面。

translations.literal: The inner usher's supervisor was set south of the host inside the inner gate, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The inner usher supervisor stood south of the host inside the inner gate, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 司贊位於東階東南，掌贊二人在南，差退，俱西向。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer was southeast of the east steps; two ritual assistants south, slightly back—all west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer stood southeast of the east steps; two assistants south, slightly back—all west-facing.

sentences.zh: 又置一桉於閤外。

translations.literal: Another table was placed outside the private gate.
translations.idiomatic: Another table was set outside the private gate.

sentences.zh: 使、副乘輅，持節，備儀仗，鼓吹備而不作。

translations.literal: Envoy and deputy rode the ceremonial chariot with staff; guards and insignia were ready but music did not play.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy rode the ceremonial chariot with staff; guards and insignia were ready but silent.

sentences.zh: 內僕進重翟以下於大門之外道西，東向，以北為上。

translations.literal: Inner servants advanced the heavy carriage and below west of the great gate outside the road, east-facing, north at the top.
translations.idiomatic: Inner servants brought the heavy carriage west of the main gate road, east-facing, north at the top.

sentences.zh: 諸衞令其屬布后儀仗。

translations.literal: Guards ordered their units to deploy the empress's guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Guards deployed the empress's honor guard.

sentences.zh: 使者出次，就位。

translations.literal: The envoy left the lodge and took his place.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy left the lodge and took station.

sentences.zh: 主人朝服立於東階下，西面。

translations.literal: The host in court dress stood below the east steps, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The host in court dress stood below the east steps, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 儐者受命，出請事。

translations.literal: The usher received the command and came out to ask business.
translations.idiomatic: The usher took orders and came out to ask business.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「某奉制，授皇后備物典冊。

translations.literal: The envoy said: "So-and-so, by edict, presents the empress's equipage, canon, and seal."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said: "So-and-so, by edict, brings the empress's equipage, investiture text, and seal."

sentences.zh: 」儐者入告，主人出迎於大門外，北面再拜，使者不答拜。

translations.literal: The usher entered to report; the host went out to meet outside the great gate, north-facing bowed twice; the envoy did not return the bow.
translations.idiomatic: The usher announced; the host met him outside the main gate, bowed twice north-facing; the envoy did not return the bow.

sentences.zh: 使者入門而左，持節者前導，持桉者次之。

translations.literal: The envoy entered the gate to the left; the staff-bearer led; the table-bearer followed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy entered left of the gate; staff-bearer first, table-bearer after.

sentences.zh: 主人入門而右，至內門外位。

translations.literal: The host entered the gate to the right, to the place inside the inner gate.
translations.idiomatic: The host entered right of the gate to the inner-gate station.

sentences.zh: 奉冊寶桉者進，授使副冊寶。

translations.literal: Those with investiture table advanced, handed investiture and seal to the deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture bearers advanced and gave text and seal to the deputy.

sentences.zh: 內侍進使者前，西面受冊寶，東面授內謁者監，持入，立於閤外之西，東面跪置於桉。

translations.literal: A eunuch advanced before the envoy, west-facing received investiture and seal, east-facing handed them to the inner usher supervisor, who carried them in, knelt west of the private gate outside, east-facing, and set them on the table.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch advanced before the envoy, received text and seal west-facing, passed them east-facing to the inner usher supervisor, who carried them in, knelt west outside the private gate, east-facing, and set them on the table.

sentences.zh: 尚宮以下入閤，奉后首飾、褘衣，傅姆贊出，尚宮引降立於庭中，北面。

translations.literal: Palace Ladies and below entered the private gate, bore the empress's head ornaments and ceremonial robe; the instructress praised her out; the Senior Palace Lady led her down to stand in the court, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ladies entered with head ornaments and ceremonial robe; the instructress presented her; the Senior Palace Lady led her down to stand in the court, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 尚宮跪取冊，尚服跪取寶綬，立於后之右，西向。

translations.literal: The Senior Palace Lady knelt, took the investiture; the Palace Wardrobe knelt, took the seal cord—both stood right of the empress, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Palace Lady knelt for the investiture text; Palace Wardrobe knelt for the seal cord—both stood right of the empress, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 司言、司寶各一人立於后左，東向。

translations.literal: Court Announcer and Court Seal-keeper each one stood left of the empress, east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Court Announcer and Court Seal-keeper each stood left of the empress, east-facing.

sentences.zh: 尚宮曰：「有制。

translations.literal: The Senior Palace Lady said: "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Palace Lady said: "By edict."

sentences.zh: 」尚儀曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Chief Palace Lady said: "Bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Palace Lady called: "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」皇后再拜。

translations.literal: " The empress bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 宣冊。

translations.literal: The investiture was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The investiture was read.

sentences.zh: 尚儀曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Chief Palace Lady said: "Bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Palace Lady called: "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」皇后又再拜。

translations.literal: " The empress bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 尚宮授皇后以冊，受以授司言。

translations.literal: The Senior Palace Lady handed the empress the investiture; she received it and handed it to the Court Announcer.
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Palace Lady gave the investiture text; the empress received it and passed it to the Court Announcer.

sentences.zh: 尚服又授以寶綬，受以授司寶。

translations.literal: Palace Wardrobe again handed the seal cord; she received it and handed it to the Court Seal-keeper.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Wardrobe gave the seal cord; she received it and passed it to the Court Seal-keeper.

sentences.zh: 皇后升坐，內官以下俱降立於庭，重行相向，西上。

translations.literal: The empress ascended the seat; inner officers all descended to stand in the court in double rows facing each other, west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: The empress took the seat; inner officers descended to the court in facing double rows, west at the top.

sentences.zh: 司贊曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer said: "Bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called: "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」掌贊承傳，皆再拜。

translations.literal: The assistants transmitted; all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Assistants relayed the call; all bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 諸應侍衞者各升，立於侍位。

translations.literal: Each attendant guard ascended and stood at attendance stations.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard attendant mounted to attendance stations.

sentences.zh: 尚儀前跪奏曰：「禮畢。

translations.literal: The Chief Palace Lady advanced kneeling and reported: "The rite is complete."
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Palace Lady knelt forward and announced the rite complete.

sentences.zh: 」皇后降坐以入。

translations.literal: The empress descended the seat and entered.
translations.idiomatic: The empress left the seat and went in.

sentences.zh: 使者復命。

translations.literal: The envoy reported back.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy returned to report.

sentences.zh: 其遣使者奉迎。

translations.literal: Dispatch of the envoy to escort and welcome her.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch of the envoy to escort and welcome her.

sentences.zh: 其日，侍中版奏「請中嚴」。

translations.literal: That day the Palace Attendant reported on the board: "Request mid-court vigil."
translations.idiomatic: That day the Palace Attendant reported: "Request mid-court vigil."

sentences.zh: 皇帝服冕出，升所御殿，文武之官五品已上立於東西朝堂。

translations.literal: The emperor in full dress came out, ascended the hall he would occupy; civil and military officials of fifth rank and above stood in the east and west audience halls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in full dress came out and mounted the hall; civil and military officials of fifth rank and above stood in the east and west audience halls.

sentences.zh: 奉迎前一日，守宮設使者次於大門之外道右，設使副及內侍次於使者次西，俱南向。

translations.literal: On the day before the escort, palace guards set the envoy's lodge east of the road outside the great gate; deputy and eunuchs west of the envoy's lodge—all south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The day before escort, guards set the envoy's lodge east of the road outside the main gate; deputy and eunuchs west of it—all south-facing.

sentences.zh: 尚舍設宮人次於閤外道西。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household set palace women's lodges west of the lane outside the private gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household set palace women's lodges west of the lane outside the private gate.

sentences.zh: 奉禮設使、副、持桉執鴈者、持節者及奉禮、贊者位，如冊后。

translations.literal: Directors of Ritual set places for envoy, deputy, table and goose bearers, staff-bearer, directors and announcers—as at empress investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual directors set stations for envoy, deputy, table and goose bearers, staff, directors, and announcers—as at investiture.

sentences.zh: 又設內侍位於大門外道左，西面。

translations.literal: Eunuchs were also set east of the road outside the great gate, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs were also placed east of the road outside the main gate, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設宮人以下位於堂前。

translations.literal: Palace women and below were also set before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women were also stationed before the hall.

sentences.zh: 使、副朝服，乘輅持節，至大門外次，宮人等各之次奉迎。

translations.literal: Envoy and deputy in court dress rode the ceremonial chariot with staff to the lodge outside the great gate; palace women each went to their lodges for the escort.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy in court dress rode the ceremonial chariot with staff to the lodge; palace women went to their escort lodges.

sentences.zh: 尚儀奏「請皇后中嚴」。

translations.literal: The Chief Palace Lady reported: "Request the empress mid-court vigil."
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Palace Lady reported: "Request the empress mid-court vigil."

sentences.zh: 傅姆導皇后，尚宮前引，出，升堂。

translations.literal: The instructress guided the empress; the Senior Palace Lady led before; she came out and ascended the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The instructress guided the empress; the Senior Palace Lady led; she came out and mounted the hall.

sentences.zh: 皇后將出，主婦出於房外之西，南向。

translations.literal: When the empress was about to go out, the hostess came out west of the outer chamber, south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress was to leave, the hostess came out west of the outer chamber, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 文武奉迎者皆陪立於大門之外，文官在東，武官在西，皆北上。

translations.literal: Civil and military escorts all stood outside the great gate; civil east, military west—all north at the top.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military escorts stood outside the main gate—civil east, military west, north at the top.

sentences.zh: 謁者引使者詣大門外位，主人立於內門外堂前東階下，西面。

translations.literal: The usher led the envoy to the place outside the great gate; the host stood below the east steps before the inner gate hall, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The usher led the envoy outside the main gate; the host stood below the east steps before the inner hall, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 儐者受命，出請事，使者曰：「某奉制，以今吉辰，率職奉迎。

translations.literal: The usher received the command, came out to ask business; the envoy said: "So-and-so, by edict, on this auspicious day bears commission to escort and welcome."
translations.idiomatic: The usher took orders and asked business; the envoy said: "So-and-so, by edict, on this auspicious day escorts and welcomes her."

sentences.zh: 」儐者入告，主人曰：「臣謹奉典制。

translations.literal: The usher entered to report; the host said: "I respectfully follow the canonical statutes."
translations.idiomatic: The usher announced; the host said: "I follow the statutes."

sentences.zh: 」儐者出告，入，引主人出門南，北面再拜。

translations.literal: The usher went out to report, entered, led the host out south of the gate, north-facing bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The usher reported, re-entered, led the host out south of the gate; he bowed twice north-facing.

sentences.zh: 謁者引入至內門外堂西階，使者先升，位於兩楹間，南面；

translations.literal: The usher led him in to the west steps of the inner gate hall; the envoy ascended first and stood between the pillars, south-facing;
translations.idiomatic: The usher brought him to the inner hall's west steps; the envoy mounted first between the pillars, south-facing;

sentences.zh: 副在西，持桉、執鴈者在西南，俱東面。

translations.literal: deputy west; table and goose bearers southwest—all east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: deputy west; table and goose bearers southwest—all east-facing.

sentences.zh: 主人升東階，詣使者前，北面立。

translations.literal: The host ascended the east steps, came before the envoy, and stood north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The host mounted the east steps and stood before the envoy, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 使、副授以制書，曰：「有制。

translations.literal: Envoy and deputy handed the edict, saying: "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy handed the edict, saying: "By edict."

sentences.zh: 」主人再拜。

translations.literal: " The host bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " The host bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 使者宣制，主人降詣階間，北面再拜稽首。

translations.literal: The envoy proclaimed the edict; the host descended between the steps, north-facing bowed twice and knocked head to ground.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy read the edict; the host went down between the steps and kowtowed north-facing.

sentences.zh: 升，進，北面受制書。

translations.literal: He ascended, advanced, and north-facing received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted, advanced, and received the edict north-facing.

sentences.zh: 主人再拜，北面立。

translations.literal: The host bowed twice and stood north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The host bowed twice and stood north-facing.

sentences.zh: 使、副授以鴈，主人再拜，進受，仍北面立。

translations.literal: Envoy and deputy handed the geese; the host bowed twice, advanced to receive, and still stood north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy presented geese; the host bowed twice, advanced to receive them, and remained north-facing.

sentences.zh: 儐者引二人對舉答表桉進，主人以表授使、副，再拜，降自西階以出，復門外位。

translations.literal: The usher led two men bearing the reply table forward; the host handed the table to envoy and deputy, bowed twice, descended the west steps to go out, and returned to the outer gate station.
translations.idiomatic: The usher led two men with the reply table; the host gave it to envoy and deputy, bowed twice, went down the west steps out, and returned outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 奉禮曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: Directors of Ritual said: "Bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual directors called: "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」贊者承傳，使、副俱再拜。

translations.literal: " Announcers transmitted; envoy and deputy both bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " Announcers relayed; envoy and deputy bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「令月吉日，臣某等承制，率職奉迎。

translations.literal: The envoy said: "On this auspicious day of the proper month, we So-and-so, by edict, bear commission to escort and welcome."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said: "On this auspicious day, we, by edict, escort and welcome her."

sentences.zh: 」內侍受以入，傳於司言，司言受以奏聞。

translations.literal: A eunuch received it to enter, transmitted to the Court Announcer, who received it and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch took it in and passed it to the Court Announcer, who reported upward.

sentences.zh: 尚儀奏請皇后再拜。

translations.literal: The Chief Palace Lady reported requesting the empress bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Palace Lady asked the empress to bow twice.

sentences.zh: 主人入，升自東階，進，西面誡之曰：「戒之敬之，夙夜無違命。

translations.literal: The host entered, ascended the east steps, advanced, and west-facing admonished her: "Be vigilant and reverent; morning and night do not disobey the command."
translations.idiomatic: The host mounted the east steps, advanced, and west-facing warned her: "Be vigilant and reverent; never disobey the command day or night."

sentences.zh: 」主人退，立於東階上，西面。

translations.literal: The host withdrew and stood on the east steps, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The host withdrew to the east steps, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 母誡於西階上，施衿結帨，曰：「勉之敬之，夙夜無違命。

translations.literal: The mother admonished on the west steps, attached collar and tied sash, saying: "Strive and be reverent; morning and night do not disobey the command."
translations.idiomatic: The mother admonished from the west steps, fixed collar and sash, saying: "Strive and be reverent; never disobey the command day or night."

sentences.zh: 」皇后升輿以降，升重翟以几，姆加景，內宮侍從及內侍導引，應乘車從者如鹵簿。

translations.literal: " The empress mounted the carriage to descend, mounted the heavy carriage with armrest, the instructress added the sunshade; inner palace attendants and eunuchs guided; those who should ride followed as in the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress mounted her carriage, then the heavy carriage with armrest; the instructress added the sunshade; inner attendants and eunuchs guided; escorts followed the imperial guard array.

sentences.zh: 皇后車出大門外，以次乘車馬引從。

translations.literal: The empress's carriage left outside the great gate; followers mounted horses and carriages in order.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's carriage left the main gate; followers mounted in order.

sentences.zh: 同牢之日，內侍之屬設皇后大次於皇帝所御殿門外之東，南向。

translations.literal: On the day of the shared meal, inner attendants set the empress's great lodge east outside the gate of the hall the emperor would occupy, south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: On the shared-meal day, inner attendants set the empress's great lodge east outside the emperor's hall gate, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 將夕，尚寢設皇帝御幄於室內之奧，東向。

translations.literal: At dusk the Imperial Chamberlain set the emperor's curtain-bed in the inner recess of the chamber, east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the Imperial Chamberlain set the emperor's bed-curtain in the chamber recess, east-facing.

sentences.zh: 鋪地席重茵，施屏障。

translations.literal: Floor mats with layered cushions were spread; screens were set.
translations.idiomatic: Layered floor mats and cushions were spread; screens were erected.

sentences.zh: 初昏，尚食設洗於東階，東西當東霤，南北以堂深。

translations.literal: At first dusk the Imperial Food Service set a lavabo on the east steps, east and west aligned with the east eaves, north-south along the depth of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At first dusk the Imperial Food Service set a lavabo on the east steps, aligned with the east eaves, running the depth of the hall.

sentences.zh: 后洗於東房，近北。

translations.literal: The empress washed in the east chamber, near the north.
translations.idiomatic: The empress washed in the east chamber near the north.

sentences.zh: 設饌於東房西墉下，籩、豆各二十四，簋、簠各二，豋各三，俎三。

translations.literal: Food was set under the west wall of the east chamber: twenty-four baskets and dishes each, two grain trays and bowls each, three tureens each, three trays.
translations.idiomatic: Food was laid under the east chamber's west wall: twenty-four baskets and dishes each, two grain trays and bowls, three tureens, three meat trays.

sentences.zh: 尊於室內北牖下，玄酒在西。

translations.literal: A wine jar under the north window inside the chamber; black wine west.
translations.idiomatic: A wine jar under the north window inside the chamber, black wine to the west.

sentences.zh: 又尊於房戶外之東，無玄酒。

translations.literal: Another jar east outside the chamber door; no black wine.
translations.idiomatic: Another jar east outside the chamber door, without black wine.

sentences.zh: 坫在南，加四爵，合巹。

translations.literal: The stand south; four goblets added; nuptial gourds joined.
translations.idiomatic: Stand to the south; four goblets added; nuptial gourds joined.

sentences.zh: 器皆烏漆，巹以匏。

translations.literal: All vessels black lacquer; the gourds in a case.
translations.idiomatic: All vessels were black lacquer; gourds in a case.

sentences.zh: 皇后入大門，鳴鍾鼓。

translations.literal: The empress entered the great gate; bells and drums sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The empress entered the main gate to bells and drums.

sentences.zh: 從永巷至大次前，回車南向，施步障。

translations.literal: From the eternal lane to before the great lodge she turned the carriage south; a walking screen was set.
translations.idiomatic: From the eternal lane to the great lodge she turned the carriage south and a walking screen was set.

sentences.zh: 尚儀進當車前，跪請降車。

translations.literal: The Chief Palace Lady advanced before the carriage, knelt, and requested she descend.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Palace Lady advanced before the carriage, knelt, and asked her to descend.

sentences.zh: 皇后降，入次。

translations.literal: The empress descended and entered the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The empress descended and entered the lodge.

sentences.zh: 尚宮引詣殿門之外，西向立。

translations.literal: The Senior Palace Lady led her to west of the hall gate and she stood west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Palace Lady led her west of the hall gate to stand west-facing.

sentences.zh: 尚儀跪奏「外辦，請降坐禮迎」。

translations.literal: The Chief Palace Lady knelt and reported: "The outer rites are ready—please descend the seat to welcome her with rite."
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Palace Lady knelt and announced: "Outer rites are ready—please leave the seat to welcome her."

sentences.zh: 皇帝降坐，尚宮前引，詣門內之西，東面揖后以入。

translations.literal: The emperor descended; the Senior Palace Lady led before, went to west inside the gate, east-facing bowed to the empress to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended; the Senior Palace Lady led him west inside the gate and east-facing bowed the empress in.

sentences.zh: 尚食酌玄酒三注於尊，尚寢設席於室內之西，東向。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service poured black wine three times into the jar; Imperial Chamberlain set the mat west inside the chamber, east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service poured black wine three times into the jar; Imperial Chamberlain set the mat west inside the chamber, east-facing.

sentences.zh: 皇帝導后升自西階，入室即席，東向立。

translations.literal: The emperor guided the empress up the west steps, entered the chamber and took the mat, standing east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor guided the empress up the west steps; they entered and took the mat, east-facing.

sentences.zh: 皇后入，立於尊西，南面。

translations.literal: The empress entered and stood west of the jar, south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress entered and stood west of the jar, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 皇帝盥於西洗，后盥於北洗。

translations.literal: The emperor washed at the west lavabo; the empress washed at the north lavabo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor washed at the west lavabo; the empress at the north lavabo.

sentences.zh: 饌入，設醬於席前，葅醢在其北；

translations.literal: Food entered; sauce was set before the mat, pickled hash north of it;
translations.idiomatic: Food was brought in; sauce before the mat, pickled hash north of it;

sentences.zh: 俎三設於豆東，豕俎特在北。

translations.literal: three trays east of the dishes; the pig tray especially north.
translations.idiomatic: three trays east of the dishes, pig tray farthest north.

sentences.zh: 尚食設黍于醬東，稷、稻、粱又在東；

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service set millet east of the sauce; glutinous, non-glutinous, and fine millet farther east;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service set millet east of the sauce, then glutinous, non-glutinous, and fine millet;

sentences.zh: 設湆于醬南。

translations.literal: broth south of the sauce.
translations.idiomatic: broth south of the sauce.

sentences.zh: 設后對醬于東，當特俎，葅醢在其南，北上；

translations.literal: The empress's sauce was set east, opposite the special pig tray; pickled hash south, north at the top;
translations.idiomatic: The empress's sauce was east, opposite the pig tray; pickled hash south, north at top;

sentences.zh: 設黍于豕俎北，其西稷、稻、粱，設湆于醬北。

translations.literal: millet north of the pig tray; west of it glutinous, non-glutinous, and fine millet; broth north of the sauce.
translations.idiomatic: millet north of the pig tray; west of it the three grains; broth north of her sauce.

sentences.zh: 尚食啟會郤于簠簋之南，對簠簋于北，加匕箸，尚寢設對席於饌東。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service opened the joint covers south of the trays and bowls, paired trays and bowls north, added spoons and chopsticks; Imperial Chamberlain set the facing mat east of the food.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service opened covers south of the trays, paired trays north, added spoons and chopsticks; Imperial Chamberlain set the facing mat east of the food.

sentences.zh: 尚食跪奏「饌具」。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service knelt and reported: "The food is ready."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service knelt and announced the food ready.

sentences.zh: 皇帝揖皇后升，對席，西面，皆坐。

translations.literal: The emperor gestured for the empress to ascend; facing mats, west-facing, both sat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor motioned the empress up; on facing mats, both sat west-facing.

sentences.zh: 尚食跪取韭葅擩醢授皇帝，取葅擩醢授皇后，俱受，祭於豆間。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service knelt, took leek hash dipped in sauce and handed to the emperor; took hash dipped in sauce and handed to the empress; both received and sacrificed between the dishes.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service knelt, dipped leek hash in sauce for the emperor and hash for the empress; both received and offered between the dishes.

sentences.zh: 尚食又取黍實於左手，遍取稷、稻、粱反於右手，授皇帝，又取黍、稷、稻粱授皇后，俱受，祭於豆間。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service again took millet in the left hand, gathered glutinous, non-glutinous, and fine millet in the right, handed to the emperor; again took the grains and handed to the empress; both received and sacrificed between the dishes.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service again put millet in the left hand, gathered the three grains in the right for the emperor, then the same for the empress; both offered between the dishes.

sentences.zh: 又各取胏絕末授帝、后，俱祭於豆間。

translations.literal: Again each took a rib end and handed to emperor and empress; both sacrificed between the dishes.
translations.idiomatic: Again each took rib ends for emperor and empress; both offered between the dishes.

sentences.zh: 尚食各以胏加於俎。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service each placed the ribs on the trays.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service set the ribs on the trays.

sentences.zh: 司飾二人以巾授皇帝及皇后，俱涗手。

translations.literal: Two dressers with towels handed to emperor and empress; both wiped hands.
translations.idiomatic: Two dressers gave towels; emperor and empress wiped their hands.

sentences.zh: 尚食各跪品嘗饌，移黍置於席上，以次授胏脊，帝、后皆食，三飯，卒食。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service each knelt, tasted the food, moved millet to the mat, then in order handed rib and spine; emperor and empress all ate, three mouthfuls, finished eating.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service each knelt, tasted the food, moved millet to the mat, then handed rib and spine in order; emperor and empress ate three mouthfuls and finished.

sentences.zh: 尚食二人俱盥手洗爵於房，入室，酌于尊，以授帝、后，俱受，祭。

translations.literal: Two Imperial Food Service officers both washed hands and rinsed goblets in the chamber, entered, poured from the jar, handed to emperor and empress; both received and sacrificed.
translations.idiomatic: Two food officers washed hands and goblets in the chamber, entered, poured from the jar, and gave to emperor and empress; both received and offered.

sentences.zh: 尚食各以肝從，皆奠爵、振祭、嚌之。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service each followed with liver; all set goblets, shook offerings, tasted.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service each followed with liver; all set goblets, shook offerings, and tasted.

sentences.zh: 尚食皆受，實於俎、豆。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service all received and placed on trays and dishes.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service received and placed them on trays and dishes.

sentences.zh: 各取爵，皆飲。

translations.literal: Each took a goblet; all drank.
translations.idiomatic: Each took a goblet and drank.

sentences.zh: 尚儀受虛爵，奠於坫。

translations.literal: The Chief Palace Lady received the empty goblets and set them on the stand.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Palace Lady took the empty goblets and set them on the stand.

sentences.zh: 再酳如初，三酳用巹，如再酳。

translations.literal: Second toast as at first; third toast used the nuptial gourds, as at the second toast.
translations.idiomatic: Second toast as before; third toast used the nuptial gourds, as the second.

sentences.zh: 尚食俱降東階，洗爵，升，酌於戶外，進，北面奠爵，興，再拜，跪取爵祭酒，遂飲卒爵，奠，遂拜，執爵興，降，奠於篚。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service both descended the east steps, washed goblets, ascended, poured outside the door, advanced, north-facing set the goblets, rose, bowed twice, knelt, took the goblet, sacrificed to the wine, then drank and finished, set it down, bowed, took the goblet, rose, descended, and set it in the basket.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service both went down the east steps, washed goblets, mounted, poured outside the door, advanced north-facing, set goblets, rose, bowed twice, knelt, took a goblet, offered to the wine, drank it off, set it down, bowed, rose, descended, and placed it in the basket.

sentences.zh: 尚儀北面跪，奏稱：「禮畢，興。

translations.literal: The Chief Palace Lady knelt north-facing and reported: "The rite is complete," and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Palace Lady knelt north-facing, announced the rite complete, and rose.

sentences.zh: 」帝、后俱興。

translations.literal: " Emperor and empress both rose.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor and empress both rose.

sentences.zh: 尚宮引皇帝入東房，釋冕服，御常服；

translations.literal: The Senior Palace Lady led the emperor into the east chamber to remove dragon robes and wear ordinary dress;
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Palace Lady led the emperor into the east chamber to remove court robes and wear ordinary dress;

sentences.zh: 尚宮引皇后入幄，脫服。

translations.literal: the Senior Palace Lady led the empress into the curtain to remove her robes.
translations.idiomatic: the Senior Palace Lady led the empress into the curtain to undress.

sentences.zh: 尚宮引皇帝入。

translations.literal: The Senior Palace Lady led the emperor in.
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Palace Lady led the emperor in.

sentences.zh: 尚食徹饌，設於東房，如初。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service cleared the food and set it in the east chamber as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service cleared the food to the east chamber as before.

sentences.zh: 皇后從者餕皇帝之饌，皇帝侍者餕皇后之饌。

translations.literal: The empress's followers ate the emperor's food; the emperor's attendants ate the empress's food.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's attendants ate the emperor's leftovers; the emperor's attendants ate the empress's.

sentences.zh: 皇太子納妃。

translations.literal: The crown prince takes a consort.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince takes a consort.

sentences.zh: 皇帝遣使者至于主人之家，不持節，無制書。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched an envoy to the host's house without staff and without an edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to the host's house without staff or edict.

sentences.zh: 其納采、問名、納吉、納徵、告期，皆如后禮。

translations.literal: Betrothal, name inquiry, auspicious acceptance, bride-price, and announcement of the date were all as for the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Betrothal, name inquiry, auspicious acceptance, bride-price, and date announcement all followed empress rites.

sentences.zh: 其冊妃。

translations.literal: Investiture of the consort.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture of the consort.

sentences.zh: 前一日，主人設使者次大門之外道右，南向；

translations.literal: On the previous day the host set the envoy's lodge east of the road outside the great gate, south-facing;
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the host set the envoy's lodge east of the road outside the main gate, south-facing;

sentences.zh: 又設宮人次於使者西南，俱東向，障以行帷。

translations.literal: palace women's lodges southwest of the envoy, all east-facing, screened by traveling curtains.
translations.idiomatic: palace women's lodges southwest of the envoy, all east-facing, behind traveling screens.

sentences.zh: 奉禮設使者位於大門外之西，副及內侍又於其南，舉冊桉及璽綬，命服者又南，差退，俱東向。

translations.literal: Directors of Ritual set the envoy west outside the great gate; deputy and eunuchs south; investiture table and seal cord, order-of-dress bearers farther south, slightly back—all east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual directors set the envoy west outside the main gate; deputy and eunuchs south; investiture table, seal cord, and order-of-dress bearers farther south, slightly back—all east-facing.

sentences.zh: 設主人位於門南，北面。

translations.literal: The host's place south of the gate, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The host's station south of the gate, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設位於內門外，如之。

translations.literal: Inside the inner gate also as above.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the inner gate, placement was the same.

sentences.zh: 設典內位於內門外主人之南，西面。

translations.literal: Palace Superintendent set south of the host inside the inner gate, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Superintendent stood south of the host inside the inner gate, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 宮人位於門外使者之後，重行東向，以北為上，障以行帷。

translations.literal: Palace women outside behind the envoy in double rows east-facing, north at the top, screened by traveling curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women behind the envoy outside in double rows, east-facing, north at top, behind traveling screens.

sentences.zh: 設贊者二人位於東階東南，西向。

translations.literal: Two announcers southeast of the east steps, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Two announcers southeast of the east steps, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 典內預置一桉於閤外。

translations.literal: Palace Superintendent pre-set a table outside the private gate.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Superintendent set a table outside the private gate beforehand.

sentences.zh: 使、副朝服，乘輅持節，鼓吹備而不作。

translations.literal: Envoy and deputy in court dress rode the ceremonial chariot with staff; musicians ready but not playing.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and deputy in court dress rode the ceremonial chariot with staff; musicians present but silent.

sentences.zh: 至妃氏大門外次，掌嚴奉褕翟衣及首飾，內廄尉進厭翟於大門之外道西，東向，以北為上。

translations.literal: At the consort's family great gate outside the lodge, Palace Strictness bore the feather carriage robe and head ornaments; Inner Stables Captain advanced the disdain carriage west of the great gate outside the road, east-facing, north at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At the consort's gate the palace strictness officer brought feather robe and ornaments; the Inner Stables Captain brought the disdain carriage west of the main gate road, east-facing, north at top.

sentences.zh: 諸衞帥其屬布儀仗。

translations.literal: Guards led their units to deploy the guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Guards deployed the honor guard.

sentences.zh: 使者出次，持節前導，及宮人、典內皆就位。

translations.literal: The envoy left the lodge; staff-bearer led; palace women and Palace Superintendent all took their places.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy left the lodge; staff-bearer led; palace women and superintendent took station.

sentences.zh: 主人朝服，出迎於大門之外，北面再拜。

translations.literal: The host in court dress went out to meet outside the great gate, north-facing bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The host in court dress met him outside the main gate and bowed twice north-facing.

sentences.zh: 使者入門而左，持桉從之。

translations.literal: The envoy entered the gate to the left; table-bearers followed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy entered left of the gate; table-bearers followed.

sentences.zh: 主人入門而右，至內門外位。

translations.literal: The host entered the gate to the right to the inner-gate station.
translations.idiomatic: The host entered right to the inner-gate station.

sentences.zh: 奉冊寶桉者進，授使副冊寶，內侍西面受之，東面授典內，典內持入，跪置於閤內之桉。

translations.literal: Investiture bearers advanced, handed text and seal to the deputy; a eunuch west-facing received, east-facing handed to Palace Superintendent, who carried them in and knelt on the table inside the private gate.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture bearers advanced and gave text and seal to the deputy; a eunuch received west-facing, passed east-facing to the superintendent, who carried them in and knelt them on the table inside the private gate.

sentences.zh: 奉衣服及侍衞者從入，皆立於典內之南，俱東面。

translations.literal: Clothing bearers and attendants followed in and all stood south of the superintendent, east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Clothing bearers and guards followed in and stood south of the superintendent, east-facing.

sentences.zh: 傅姆贊妃出，立於庭中，北面。

translations.literal: The instructress praised the consort out; she stood in the court, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The instructress presented the consort; she stood in the court, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 掌書跪取玉寶，南向。

translations.literal: Chief Scribe knelt, took the jade seal, south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Scribe knelt and took the jade seal, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 掌嚴奉首飾、褕翟，與諸宮官侍衞者以次入。

translations.literal: Palace Strictness bore head ornaments and feather robe; palace officers and guards entered in order.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Strictness brought head ornaments and feather robe; palace officers and guards entered in order.

sentences.zh: 司則前贊妃再拜，北面受冊寶於掌書，南向授妃，妃以授司閨。

translations.literal: Chief Steward advanced praising the consort bow twice; north-facing she received investiture and seal from the Chief Scribe, south-facing handed to the consort, and the consort gave them to the Court Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Steward praised her to bow twice; north-facing she received text and seal from the Chief Scribe, south-facing gave them to the consort, and the consort passed them to the Court Chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 司則又贊再拜，乃請妃升坐。

translations.literal: Chief Steward again praised bow twice, then asked the consort ascend the seat.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Steward praised bow twice again, then asked the consort to take the seat.

sentences.zh: 宮官以下皆降立於庭，重行，北面西上。

translations.literal: Palace officers all descended to stand in the court in double rows, north-facing with west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: Palace officers descended to the court in double rows, north-facing, west at top.

sentences.zh: 贊者曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The announcer said: "Bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called: "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」皆再拜。

translations.literal: " All bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " All bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 司則前啟「禮畢」。

translations.literal: Chief Steward advanced and announced "the rite is complete."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Steward announced the rite complete.

sentences.zh: 妃降座，入於室。

translations.literal: The consort descended the seat and entered the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The consort left the seat and entered the chamber.

sentences.zh: 主人儐使者如禮賓之儀。

translations.literal: The host entertained the envoy as in receiving a guest of honor.
translations.idiomatic: The host entertained the envoy per guest-of-honor rites.

sentences.zh: 臨軒醮戒。

translations.literal: Facing-the-hall libation and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Facing-the-hall libation and admonition.

sentences.zh: 前一日，衞尉設次於東朝堂之北，西向。

translations.literal: On the previous day the Commandant of Guards set a lodge north of the east audience hall, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the Commandant of Guards set a lodge north of the east audience hall, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設宮官次於重明門外。

translations.literal: Palace officers' lodges were also set outside the Chongming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Palace officers' lodges were set outside the Chongming Gate as well.

sentences.zh: 其日，皇太子服衮冕出，升金輅，至承天門降輅，就次。

translations.literal: That day the crown prince in dragon robes came out, mounted the golden carriage to the Chengtian Gate, descended, and went to the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: That day the crown prince in dragon robes mounted the golden carriage to Chengtian Gate, descended, and went to the lodge.

sentences.zh: 前一日，有司設御座於太極殿阼階上，西向。

translations.literal: On the previous day the relevant offices set the imperial seat on the steps of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, officials set the imperial seat on the Hall of Supreme Ultimate steps, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 設羣官次於朝堂，展縣，陳車輅。

translations.literal: Officials' lodges were set in the audience hall; bells hung and carriages arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' lodges were set in the audience hall; bells hung and carriages lined up.

sentences.zh: 其日，尚舍設皇太子席位於戶牖間，南向，莞席、藻席。

translations.literal: That day the Imperial Household set the crown prince's mat between the door panels, south-facing, rush and painted mats.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Imperial Household set the crown prince's mat between the door panels, south-facing, rush and painted mats.

sentences.zh: 尚食設酒尊於東序下，又陳籩脯一、豆醢一，在尊西。

translations.literal: Imperial Food Service set the wine jar under the east wing; one basket of dried meat and one dish of hash west of the jar.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food Service set the wine jar under the east wing with one basket of dried meat and one dish of hash west of it.

sentences.zh: 晡前三刻，設羣官版位於內，奉禮設版位於外，如朝禮。

translations.literal: Three quarters before dusk, officials' board stations were set inside; Directors of Ritual set board stations outside, as at audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: Three quarters before dusk, officials' board stations were set inside; ritual directors set stations outside, as at audience.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏「請中嚴」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported on the board: "Request mid-court vigil."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported: "Request mid-court vigil."

sentences.zh: 前三刻，諸侍衞之官侍中、中書令以下俱詣閤奉迎。

translations.literal: Three quarters before, attendant guards including Palace Attendant and Secretariat Director all went to the private gate to escort.
translations.idiomatic: Three quarters before, attendant guards including Palace Attendant and Secretariat Director went to the private gate to escort.

sentences.zh: 典儀帥贊者先入就位，吏部、兵部贊羣官出次，就門外位。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies led announcers in first to take places; Personnel and War Ministries led officials out of lodges to outer gate stations.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies led announcers in first; Personnel and War Ministries led officials from lodges to outer stations.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏「外辦」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported on the board: "The outer rites are ready."
